Theorem
[Local maximum principle] 1. ch9:9.20\group chapter-9Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0256 Let $u\in W^{2,n}(\Omega )$ satisfy $Lu\ge f$ with $f\in L^n(\Omega )$. For every $B_{2R}(y)\subset \Omega $ and $p>0$, \begin{equation} \tag {9.48} \sup _{B_R(y)}u\le C\left[ \left(\frac1{|B_{2R}|}\int _{B_{2R}(y)}(u^+)^p\right)^{1/p} +\frac R\lambda \| f\| _{L^n(B_{2R}(y))}\right], \end{equation} where $C=C(n,\gamma ,\nu R^2,p)$.
Proof

\sketch Scale to the unit ball and set

\begin{equation} \tag {9.49} \eta (x)=(1-|x|^2)^\beta , \qquad v=\eta u. \end{equation}

On the upper contact set of $v$, concavity controls $Du$ by a multiple of $(1-|x|^2)^{-1}u$. Lemma 12 then bounds $\sup v$ by an $L^n$ norm of a power of $u^+$ and the inhomogeneous term. Choose $\beta =2n/p$ and use Young’s inequality; larger $p$ follows from a smaller exponent. Approximation gives the result for $W^{2,n}$ solutions.

□
